Job Title: Senior Scientist in Centre for Structure & Interactions

Department: Centre for Structure & Interactions, Therapeutics Discovery, Research & Development

Location: Måløv, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As a Senior Scientist in our Centre for Structure & Interactions, you will turn molecular understanding into better drug candidates for people living with serious chronic diseases. Working hands-on in the laboratory, you will develop and apply biochemical and biophysical approaches to characterise protein interactions, including those involving challenging targets such as integral membrane proteins. Your insights will guide molecular design, enable high-throughput screening and help research teams across our modality portfolio select the most promising candidates to advance.

What you’ll bring

You are a hands-on protein scientist who combines scientific curiosity with rigorous experimental judgement and the initiative to tackle challenging questions. You will bring:

• A completed PhD in protein biochemistry, protein engineering, structural biology, biophysics or a closely related discipline, or at least five years of relevant industry experience demonstrating comparable scientific depth and independence.

• Demonstrated expertise in developing and interpreting biochemical and biophysical assays with purified proteins, using methods such as surface plasmon resonance (SPR), biolayer interferometry (BLI) or fluorescence-based in vitro assays. You can assess protein quality, recognise assay limitations and draw sound mechanistic conclusions.

• A strong foundation in protein biochemistry and experience in protein engineering, such as construct optimisation, mutagenesis or investigating sequence–function relationships, together with familiarity with natural and engineered protein binders.

• Evidence of scientific excellence and independent contributions, demonstrated through high-quality publications or significant achievements in industrial research.

• Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to turn complex findings into clear recommendations and build productive relationships across disciplines and with internal and external partners.

Desirable, but not essential:

• Experience with directed evolution, display technologies or other protein selection systems.

• Experience working with challenging proteins, including integral membrane proteins, and an understanding of how preparation and handling affect their stability and activity.

• Experience in structural biology, or the ability to integrate interaction data with structural insights to guide molecular design.

• Experience with, or a strong interest in, automation, high-throughput workflows and computational tools for molecular modelling and visualisation.

What you’ll do

You will combine substantial hands-on laboratory work with scientific ownership of protein interaction studies, working closely with colleagues in the Centre and multidisciplinary project teams.

• Shape scientific questions and experimental strategies that support molecular design and drug candidate selection across our modality portfolio.

• Design, conduct and critically interpret biochemical and biophysical experiments to understand protein interactions, including those involving challenging targets such as integral membrane proteins.

• Apply your understanding of protein biochemistry, engineering and binder formats to guide experimental design and interpret molecular behaviour.

• Develop and deploy high-throughput screening assays, with careful attention to protein quality, assay performance and the biological relevance of the results.

• Develop and implement new approaches to protein interaction analysis, addressing scientific and technical challenges.

• Integrate your findings with complementary project data to provide clear recommendations and influence research decisions.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Centre for Structure & Interactions, a well-established area at the heart of Therapeutics Discovery in Research & Development. We play a central role in identifying, optimising and characterising drug candidates across all therapy areas, shaping project direction and informing key research decisions.

Your closest colleagues will be an interdisciplinary team of 18 highly skilled scientists and laboratory technicians, combining high scientific standards with a supportive, collaborative culture. Together, we connect molecular structure, function and interactions to generate insights that guide molecular design and candidate selection.

You will also work closely with multidisciplinary project teams and colleagues across our global research sites. This offers a strong scientific network and opportunities to influence research beyond your own experiments. Our colleagues bring diverse backgrounds and nationalities, and English is our working and social language.

What you can expect here

You will have the opportunity to investigate challenging molecular questions, develop new experimental approaches and shape decisions that advance promising drug candidates. Working alongside skilled colleagues across disciplines, you will contribute your expertise and ideas in an environment with high scientific standards and a shared commitment to improving patients’ lives.

We value rigorous science, open discussion and a willingness to test new ideas. You will find support to learn from experiments, develop your expertise and take increasing scientific responsibility, within a team that approaches challenges together.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,000.00 to 956,900.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Job Title: Director, Safety Operations

Department: Safety Operations, Global Patient Safety, Research & Development

Location: Søborg, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As Director, Safety Operations, you will lead the Centre of Expertise and Submission area and shape how safety information moves from affiliates to health authorities. As Novo grows, you will challenge current ways of working and drive automation and simplification, while keeping quality, compliance and timely reporting uncompromised. Your work helps make sure the safety of our treatments is understood and acted on, for the people who rely on them every day.

What you’ll bring

You are an experienced pharmacovigilance leader who combines deep regulatory knowledge with a drive to make operations simpler, faster and more scalable. You will bring:

• A master’s degree in life sciences.

• Extensive pharmacovigilance experience in a large-scale pharmaceutical company, including senior specialist roles.

• Extensive knowledge of international pharmacovigilance legislation and guidelines.

• Proven success optimising processes and systems, with solid knowledge of the business processes and IT systems behind efficient day-to-day safety operations.

• Strong people leadership experience, including leading through other leaders, and the professional authority to set direction.

• Strong communication, negotiation and conflict-management skills, and the ability to analyse and handle complex, urgent or sensitive issues calmly.

• A strategic mindset, the ability to inspire others and the willingness to take tough decisions for the benefit of the wider organisation.

Useful, but not essential:

• Hands-on experience implementing automation in case processing or regulatory submissions.

• Experience working across global hubs or influencing new regulatory requirements in external working groups.

What you’ll do

You will lead the daily operations of the Safety Operations Centre of Expertise and Submissions while setting the future direction for the area. Leading through a manager and directly managing Safety Operations specialists, you will align teams, resolve operational challenges and deliver sustainable improvements across Safety Operations. More specifically, you will:

• Lead the establishment, maintenance and continuous optimisation of end-to-end individual case safety report (ICSR) handling for clinical and post-marketing products, from affiliate intake through regulatory submission.

• Take an end-to-end view of case processing and submissions, challenge current practices and drive operational efficiency, simplification and automation while maintaining quality, compliance and timely regulatory reporting.

• Ensure systems and processes for reporting safety information remain up to date and compliant with regulatory requirements and guidelines, while influencing emerging requirements for safety information handling.

• Build a strong network across headquarters, affiliates and external collaborators, and ensure new procedures and processes are communicated clearly across the worldwide pharmacovigilance organisation.

• Ensure a consistent approach to onboarding and training across Safety Operations, with clear roles and responsibilities that are understood across the organisation.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Safety Operations, part of Global Patient Safety in Research & Development, and report to the VP of Safety Operations. Safety Operations makes sure safety information from clinical development and marketed products is collected, evaluated, processed and reported accurately, in line with global pharmacovigilance requirements. As Novo grows, the team is developing its operating model, systems and data capabilities to support scalability and efficiency.

You will lead a team of around 20 people: the manager of the global submissions team and approximately six Safety Operations specialists who report directly to you. You will secure operational excellence across organisational units in Denmark, the US and Bangalore, India.

Your network will be broad. Internally, you will work with areas across Global Patient Safety, global project teams, Global Trial Portfolio, Enterprise IT, AI and Digital Innovation, regions and affiliates, US Patient Safety, Quality, Finance, Corporate Legal and senior management. Externally, you will interact directly with health authorities, investigators and vendors. These relationships let you move decisions forward quickly and scale improvements globally.

What you can expect here

This is a role with real decision-making authority. You will be trusted to prioritise, resolve issues and delegate independently, and to set objectives that create impact across functions inside and outside Global Patient Safety. You will work in a complex, fast-moving regulatory environment where your voice shapes how safety operations evolve – and where curiosity about automation and simpler ways of working is valued.

You will be part of a culture that values clear priorities, honest feedback and never compromising on patient safety, with opportunities to grow through cross-functional work, global collaboration and relevant learning offerings.

Lead Negotiation and Contract Advisor

Job description

Location

Høje Tåstrup, Denmark

Job category

Sourcing & Procurement

Department: Negotiation and Contract Management  (Global Manufacturing & Supply)

Your impact begins here

Do you have a passion for negotiating contracts and the right business acumen required for deal-making? Are you looking for an exciting opportunity to apply your negotiation and project management skills at the highest level and on a global scale? If your answer is yes, then you could be the new Lead Negotiation and Contract Advisor we are looking for to join our Negotiation and Contract Management team.  Apply today and join us for a life-changing career!

What you’ll bring

To succeed in this role, you bring:

• A Master’s degree in Business Administration, Economics, (Commercial) Law, Supply Chain Management or a related field.

• 5+ years of commercial negotiation experience – including elements like business models, cost/price modelling, forecasting models and similar.

• Advanced contract drafting skills.

• Strong project management experience.

• Excellent stakeholder management.

• Strong English communication and presentation skills.

• A dedicated business acumen mindset.

• A strong drive and a can-do attitude.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience in a regulated industry, such as pharmaceuticals, medical devices, life sciences or food manufacturing.

What you’ll do

As Lead Negotiation & Contract Advisor, you will be leading contract discussions across a wide portfolio of potential and current suppliers of raw materials, finished products, devices and contract manufacturing services. You will be responsible for:

• Planning and timely carrying out process compliant negotiations, ensuring the outcome works for the business, today and over the life of the contract.

• The best commercial outcome for Novo Nordisk – and the millions of customers relying on our health portfolio.

• Proactively identifying solutions to commercial and legal challenges and securing cooperation and involvement from relevant internal (and external) stakeholders.

• Understanding the commercial needs of the business and transforming that to actionable key terms in the negotiation, identifying the appropriate business models and anchoring it in contracts.

• Being a professional ambassador of Novo Nordisk and ensure that negotiations are conducted in a professional way.

• Coaching and training stakeholders in negotiation processes and strategy.

• Providing strong project management of the entire contract process (and the team assigned to support the contract process) from first draft to signing.

• Obtain negotiation mandates and give management a clear view of objectives, scenarios, risks and expected value.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Negotiation and Contract Management team, which is part of the Strategy, Sourcing & Negotiation Centre of Excellence - a team of more than 20 professionals with extensive experience in running tenders and negotiating high-profile contracts. The CoE is part of the central sourcing unit in Global Manufacturing & Supply, where colleagues work across the value chain to scale molecules, processes, devices and products for Novo Nordisk’s production.

On each negotiation, you will work closely with especially Category Management and Legal colleagues, aligning with management on mandates, priorities and approvals.

What we offer

At Novo Nordisk, you will join a global healthcare company with a distinctive culture and a strong track record. We offer continuous learning, career development and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Job Title: SVP Personal Assistant

Department: Global P&O Services & Workforce Enablement, People, Organisation & Corporate Affairs

Location: Bagsværd, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As SVP Personal Assistant, you will help the SVP of Global P&O Services & Workforce Enablement stay focused on what matters most. You will manage complex priorities with discretion, anticipate what is coming and coordinate the leadership meetings, events and business processes that keep a global area moving. Your work gives leaders the time and clarity to make decisions, and gives you a real opportunity to shape how administrative excellence is delivered across Novo.

What you’ll bring

You take pride in helping senior leaders perform at their best. You work with a high degree of independence and good judgement, and you are trusted with confidential matters. You will likely bring:

• At least 5 years of experience in administrative support roles, including complex calendar management, travel coordination and cross-functional collaboration.

• A highly structured and organised approach, combined with a genuine interest in the business that helps you understand the SVP’s priorities, anticipate needs and stay ahead of upcoming demands.

• Proven ability to work independently, improve processes and mentor colleagues, with demonstrated indirect leadership skills.

• Discretion and loyalty in handling confidential information.

• An efficient, service-minded and flexible way of working, with a practical, problem-solving mindset and a proactive, change-ready approach.

• A way of working that reflects how we work at Novo: clear priorities, decisive follow-through, honest feedback, respect and integrity.

• Fluency in English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience with IT systems, SharePoint site management and onboarding processes.

What you’ll do

You will be the SVP’s trusted administrative partner, with significant autonomy over how the work gets done. Alongside the day-to-day support, you will help the wider administrative community work smarter.

You’ll be:

• Providing proactive, confidential and highly independent administrative support to the SVP, including complex calendar management, travel coordination and executive support, while working closely with the Executive Assistant and the P&O Business Partner to ensure smooth day-to-day operations.

• Acting as ambassador and trusted representative for the SVP and the Global P&O Services & Workforce Enablement area, helping drive collaboration and alignment across functions and stakeholders.

• Coordinating SVP-level leadership meetings, off-sites and townhalls together with the Executive Assistant, as well as independently coordinating cross-functional activities and events.

• Collaborating with leaders and stakeholders on annual business processes, including budget planning.

• Acting as proxy/delegate in relevant IT systems and supporting governance of department and area collaboration platforms, including SharePoint and Microsoft 365 solutions.

• Driving continuous improvement of administrative processes, ways of working and digital solutions, while providing functional leadership, mentoring and knowledge sharing across the PA and administrative community.

Who you’ll work with

Global P&O Services & Workforce Enablement enables Novo to win by delivering seamless, efficient and future-fit people experiences at global scale. We combine high-quality, standardised people services with strategic talent acquisition, workforce intelligence and digital enablement to support leaders and employees across the organisation. Our area brings together People Services, Talent Acquisition, Digital Solutions, Processes & AI, and Workforce Intelligence, providing the capabilities, insights and solutions needed to help Novo perform, adapt and grow.

You will be based at our headquarters in Denmark, working closely with the SVP, the SVP leadership team, the Executive Assistant, The Sr. P&O Business Partner, the wider administrative community and key stakeholders across the organisation. This is a role where trust, discretion and collaboration are at the heart of everything you do, and where you will have a genuine opportunity to shape how administrative excellence is delivered across a global organisation.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take ownership, use your judgement and make your voice heard. Beyond supporting one senior leader, you will have the opportunity to shape how administrative work is done across a global area, through process improvement, digital ways of working and mentoring colleagues in the PA community.

You will work close to the teams that design people services, talent acquisition and digital people tools for colleagues across Novo, giving you a broad view of how a global organisation develops its people. We offer continuous learning, career development and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Medical & Translational Science

**[Søborg]

Your impact begins here

As Medical Project Director, you will help shape our cardiovascular therapy area strategy and provide medical and scientific input to business development opportunities. You will combine detailed assessment of individual assets with a portfolio perspective on what we need to develop over the next five and ten years. Working with colleagues across the value chain, you will identify opportunities, assess risks and uncertainties, and turn scientific and strategic insights into clear recommendations for leadership and portfolio decisions.

What you’ll bring

You bring strong medical and scientific expertise and sound strategic judgement. You can zoom in to understand the details and uncertainties in a dataset and zoom out to assess what they mean for an opportunity and the wider portfolio. You distinguish what the evidence supports from what remains uncertain, challenge assumptions constructively and make balanced recommendations when information is incomplete.

• A Medical Doctor degree and strong research experience at PhD level or equivalent are mandatory.

• A minimum of five years of clinical development experience is expected, together with the ability to critically assess preclinical and clinical evidence. Experience with cardiovascular disease is an advantage.

• A strong understanding of the pharmaceutical value chain, including how research, clinical development, regulatory requirements, CMC and commercial considerations influence development and portfolio decisions.

• Experience in business development or therapy area strategy is preferred. Hands-on business development experience assessing individual assets, for example through screening or due diligence, is particularly valuable.

• Experience guiding work across functions, engaging senior leaders and building agreement around priorities without relying on formal authority.

• Strong communication, presentation and collaboration skills, with the ability to explain complex scientific issues clearly in written and spoken English to colleagues with different professional backgrounds.

• Experience engaging external medical and scientific experts to inform development strategies and interpretation of evidence would be useful.

What you’ll do

• Help shape cardiovascular therapy area strategy and portfolio priorities over the next five and ten years, identifying gaps and opportunities for internal development and external innovation.

• Provide medical and scientific input to screening and due diligence of potential business development opportunities, assessing biological rationale, evidence for clinical benefit, potential differentiation, and key risks and uncertainties.

• Identify and prioritise opportunities for additional indications, considering scientific evidence, unmet medical need, the competitive landscape and the feasibility of development.

• Integrate input from colleagues across the value chain into recommendations that reflect clinical and regulatory pathways, development timelines, manufacturing considerations and commercial potential.

• Prepare clear assessments and recommendations for senior leadership and governance discussions, explaining assumptions, trade-offs and the evidence needed to resolve uncertainties and support decisions.

• Reassess portfolio priorities as new data and external developments emerge, and coordinate with colleagues to turn strategic recommendations into agreed actions and plans.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Medical & Science, Cardiovascular & Liver Disease within Medical & Translational Science and report directly to the Senior Director. This is a specialist role without line management responsibility, with leadership exercised through expertise and collaboration.

You will work closely with cardiovascular leadership, Global Project Teams and colleagues in Research, Clinical Development, Business Development, Commercial, Regulatory Affairs and CMC. You may also engage external medical experts and research partners to inform scientific assessments. Across these relationships, you will listen openly, bring different perspectives together and build the agreement needed to move strategies and plans forward.

What you can expect here

You can expect a high degree of independence, complex scientific and strategic questions, and the opportunity to influence decisions with substantial portfolio and business impact. You will take initiative, follow through on agreed actions and contribute to a collaborative environment where colleagues share knowledge and challenge each other constructively.

We will provide relevant training, onboarding and support to help you grow into the role and further develop your skills in therapy area strategy and business development. You will build on your medical and scientific experience while learning from colleagues across the value chain. Priorities may change as new evidence emerges, and you will help the team adapt its recommendations and plans.

As Research Scientist, you will build the engineered mammalian cell lines and cellular assays that help our project teams identify and select drug candidates. You will turn biological questions into robust, reproducible in vitro data that teams can act on with confidence. Working across multiple projects in Therapeutics Discovery, you will help move research forward today, supporting the search for new treatment options for people living with diabetes, obesity and other serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You combine hands-on expertise in cell line engineering with a strong understanding of what makes a cellular assay reliable and fit for purpose.

• 
A PhD in cell biology, molecular biology, biotechnology, pharmacology or a related discipline.

• 
Proven expertise in mammalian cell culture, stable cell line generation, clonal isolation and functional cell line characterisation.

• 
Experience with engineered cell lines and cellular assays, such as reporter gene, receptor binding, target engagement, flow cytometry and/or high-content imaging assays.

• 
Knowledge of assay optimisation and validation.

• 
Excellent communication skills and the ability to build and maintain relationships, both internally and externally.

• 
Curiosity, a proactive mindset and openness to new ideas, people and challenges – and a habit of sharing knowledge and giving and receiving feedback.

• 
Expertise in advanced single-cell cloning, clonal-selection technologies and genetic characterisation of KO/KI cell lines (a strong advantage).

• 
Experience with automated liquid handling systems and high-throughput screening.

What you’ll do

Your work will give project teams the cell-based models and assay data they need to make clear decisions about which drug candidates to take forward.

• 
Design, develop and characterise engineered mammalian cell lines for drug discovery and screening.

• 
Apply molecular and cellular biology techniques, including transfection, viral transduction, CRISPR/Cas9 editing, and clonal selection.

• 
Establish robust, reproducible and fit-for-purpose cellular assays that support drug candidate identification and selection.

• 
Plan, prioritise and coordinate with screening, automation, in vivo pharmacology and project teams to advance cell-based models and screening strategies.

• 
Represent the department across a range of projects and help drive research project progression.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Centre for Functional Assays & Screening (CFAS), part of Therapeutics Discovery in Måløv, Denmark. CFAS designs and runs a range of biologically relevant medium- and high-throughput screening assays, with a strong focus on automation and digitalisation. The team delivers high-quality in vitro data to support the identification, optimisation and characterisation of drug candidates across multiple projects.

CFAS consists of three sub-departments with 20 scientists at different levels of seniority, 15 laboratory technicians and two PhD students. Day to day, you will work closely with department scientists, laboratory technicians and cross-functional project teams. Because CFAS operates in a matrix organisation, you will also partner with screening, automation and in vivo pharmacology colleagues, and connect with colleagues across our global research sites – combining different expertise to keep projects moving.

Your manager will be Assoc. Director Simon Erlendsson.

What you can expect here

You will be part of a high-performing, multidisciplinary team where knowledge-sharing and feedback are part of how the work gets done. Your expertise will be heard across projects, and you will be trusted to shape the cell-based models and screening strategies teams rely on.

The environment is dynamic and evolving, with close links to automation and digitalisation. Working with colleagues across global research sites gives you the opportunity to build a strong scientific network and grow your skills through practical, cross-project experience.

The Department of Science Education at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a 2-year postdoctoral position starting 1 March 2027. The postdoc position will be a part of the SPINE project (Strengthening Pathways and Infrastructures for Navigating Interdisciplinary Collaboration in Existing Academic Structures), funded by the Lundbeck Foundation

  We are looking for an engaged and independent researcher to help us develop and test practical ways of strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration in research and education.

  The SPINE project investigates how interdisciplinary collaboration can be better supported within existing academic structures. The project combines qualitative research, international fieldwork, and participatory action research to develop practical “plug-and-play” tools, such as methods, templates, games, and workshop formats, that can be readily used by researchers, educators, and research organisations.

   

  Your role

  As a postdoc in SPINE, you will lead the testing and refinement of tools and methods at SPINE’s test sites, including designing and facilitating intervention workshops with researchers and other stakeholders. You will evaluate and adapt approaches across different contexts and help turn research findings into practical, “plug-and-play” resources for interdisciplinary collaboration.

  The position combines research and reporting on the development and testing activities with qualitative research, but the main emphasis will be on the development, testing, and refinement of practical tools and interventions.

   

  You will also contribute to:

   	
• Conducting qualitative research and fieldwork 	
• Analysing and evaluating empirical material and interventions 	
• Working with project partners and stakeholders 	
• Disseminating findings through academic and practice-oriented outputs 	
• Teaching at the Department of Science Education   The position is based in Denmark, where most work will take place. Some international travel will be required for fieldwork, test-site visits, and collaboration with project partners.

   

  Who we are looking for

  We are looking for a researcher interested in how interdisciplinary collaboration works in practice, with the ability to move between research, facilitation, and development.

   

  You should have:

   	
• The ability to work independently while contributing actively to a collaborative team 	
• Strong written and oral communication skills 	
• Willingness and ability to travel internationally when required    

  We are particularly interested in candidates with experience in one or more of the following:

   	
• Interdisciplinary higher education research 	
• Participatory action research or co-design 	
• Workshop facilitation and stakeholder engagement 	
• Developing or evaluating practical approaches to research and collaboration 	
• Translating research into practical or policy-relevant outputs 	
• Spoken or written Danish, which is an advantage but not a requirement   We welcome candidates from different disciplinary and methodological backgrounds and do not expect applicants to meet every criterion.

   

  What we offer

  You will join an international and collaborative research environment in central Copenhagen and become part of a project with a strong focus on research that makes a practical difference.

  The SPINE project is led by Associate Professor Katrine Ellemose Lindvig at the Section for Higher Education Research and Development, Department of Science Education, University of Copenhagen. The SPINE team consists of the PI, one postdoc, and one PhD student, and works closely with colleagues in a wider research group on Interdisciplinary Higher Education, which includes an additional PhD student. As postdoc, you will work closely together with the researchers in SPINE and this wider group, while also collaborating with external partners and stakeholders.

   

  Application

  Start date: 1 March 2027
 Application deadline: 28 October 2026, 23:59 CET
  

  Please submit a single application of no more than 2 pages, combining:

   	
• Your motivation and qualifications for the position, including your relevant research, methodological, and facilitation experience. 	
• Your ideas for contributing to SPINE, including how you would approach testing and refining tools and methods, designing intervention workshops, and developing practical “plug-and-play” resources.    

  In addition, please include:

   	
• CV, including research, fieldwork, teaching, and project experience 	
• One publication that best demonstrates your research capabilities and fit with the position 	
• Publication list 	
• Diplomas and transcripts 	
• Contact details for two references   Applications must be submitted in English through the University of Copenhagen's online recruitment system.

  Before applying, prospective applicants are welcome to contact Associate Professor Katrine Ellemose Lindvig to discuss the position and how their experience might fit the project.
 
 Contact:
 Katrine Ellemose Lindvig
 Email: Katrine.lindvig@ind.ku.dk
  

  The University of Copenhagen is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates.

How can the distribution grid be made more resilient? 

You have the opportunity to investigate how island operation of the distribution grid can mitigate severe incidents in the power system. Your project will be one of three PhDs in collaboration with DTU Space and DTU Electro. Your project will focus on how improved situational awareness can improve supply of prioritized loads by operating of parts of the distribution grid in island mode during interruptions.

Responsibilities and qualifications
You will in the PhD project develop methods for enhancing the ability of microgrids and distribution systems to dynamically transition to and operate as islanded grids that are controlled robustly in a no-single-point-of-failure architecture. The research will investigate how conventional grid measurements can be combined with non-traditional information sources, including information from distributed energy resources or physical surveillance data to maintain a continuously updated understanding of system state, resource availability, and network topology. Operating strategies that can accommodate continuously changing resource situations and stability threats will be devised. To afford manageability of this ever-changing system situation and communication with grid operators and non-grid emergency procedures, a self-representing explainable data model for the coordination with grid operators and other entities.

The outcomes will contribute to the development of resilient distribution system operation concepts and intelligent energy management systems capable of supporting secure islanded operation, faster system recovery, and improved security of electricity supply.

You will be part of an international group and will have the opportunity to collaborate with industry and international research groups. jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a 3 year position starting on February 1st 2027, or as soon as possible hereafter.

  This post-doc project aims at developing analytical methods to identify and quantify gangliosides and glucosylsphingosine and to combine them with existing methods available at the Lipidomics Core Facility at the Danish Cancer Institute (DCI) to analyse post-mortem brain samples and stem cell derived brain cells from patients with Parkinson’s Disease in order to identify lipid changes associated with the disease pathology.

  Information on the department can be found at: https://drug.ku.dk

   

  Our research

  The project will be anchored at the Galvagnion group and be in collaboration with Dr Mesut Bilgin and Dr Kenji Maeda at the Lipidomics Core Facility at the DCI.

  The Galvagnion group research aims at understanding the role of dysfunctions in lipid homeostasis in the emergence of neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s Diseases. Our approach consists in identifying, using biological models, lipid changes associated with these diseases and/or their risk factors and in using biophysical methods to provide at the molecular level the mechanism by which these lipid changes can influence functional protein-membrane interactions and protein aggregation. The different biological models that we consider vary in their complexity and include patient derived cells and brain materials. Our interdisciplinary research involves an international collaborative network including neuroscientists, stem cell biologists, biochemists, protein biophysicists and experts in lipidomics and proteomics.

  The main methods/techniques that we routinely use in the laboratory include molecular biology, recombinant protein production/purification; characterisation of protein, protein-membrane interactions and self/co-assembly using circular dichroism, fluorescence spectroscopy, calorimetry, electron microscopy; lipids extraction and characterisation using mass spectrometry; cell culture (established and iPS cell lines), Immunocytochemistry, Western Blot, qPCR; organelle and ex-vivo material isolation.

  We are an international group of 8 PhD students/post-doc/MSc and exchange students with expertise in protein and lipid biophysics, stem cell biology, biochemistry and proteomics.

  More information on our research can be found here:

   	
• Group website 	
• Google Scholar   The Lipidomics Core Facility, headed by Dr. Mesut Bilgin since its establishment in 2015, is a state-of-the-art mass spectrometry platform for the quantitative analysis of lipids in biological samples. Equipped with Orbitrap-based instrumentation for both shotgun and LC-MS lipidomics, the facility identifies and quantifies more than 400 lipid species across 44 lipid classes in materials ranging from cells and tissues to body fluids and organelles. The facility supports in-house research and national and international collaborations and also offers its services to external academic and industry partners. Its research focuses on the roles of lipid metabolism in cancer, including how obesity-related, adipocyte-secreted lipids reprogram the lipidome of cancer cells.

   

  Your job
 We are looking for an outstanding and passionate scientist who has a strong background in lipid analyses and method development. This post-doc project aims at developing new methods to identify and quantify gangliosides and glucosyl and galactosyl sphingosine and to use them in combination with existing methods available at the Lipidomics Core Facility at the DCI to determine lipid changes associated with Parkinson’s Disease in post-mortem brain homogenates, stem cell derived brain cells from patients with PD as well as aggregates isolated from these biological samples.

  The project is funded by a Novo Nordisk Ascending Investigator grant.

   

  Profile 
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills:

   	
• You hold a PhD in analytical chemistry, chemistry, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, molecular life sciences, or a related field. 	
• You have practical experience with LC-MS-based analysis of small molecules, such as lipids, metabolites, or related biomolecules. 	
• You have experience in developing and/or optimizing LC-MS methods and are able to plan, perform, and troubleshoot analytical experiments independently. 	
• You have experience working with biological samples and standard biochemical sample preparation methods. 	
• You have an interest in lipid metabolism and its role in neuroscience and neurodegenerative diseases. 	
• You have strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary team. 	
• You have excellent written and spoken English.   Desirable experience and skills:

   	
• Experience with lipidomics and/or MS-based lipid analysis. 	
• Experience working with cells, tissues, subcellular fractions, or other complex biological samples. 	
• Knowledge of Parkinson’s disease, neurodegeneration, or protein amyloid/aggregation.    

  Place of employment

  The place of employment is at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and state of the art lipidomic facilities.

   

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

Currently, the monthly salary starts at 39,900 DKK/approx. 5,300 EUR (August 2026-level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18,07 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

   

  Questions

 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. • Translate composite technology and material requirements into practical production parameters, SOPs, and work instructions.

• Degree in Engineering (BSc or MSc) in Materials, Mechanical, Chemical, Manufacturing, Composite Engineering, or equivalent strong industrial experience.

• Hands-on experience with processes such as resin infusion/transfer, filament winding, lay-up, prepreg, molding, curing, or composite machining/finishing.

• Proven experience creating or improving SOPs, work instructions, and manufacturing standards.

• Background in industrialization, production ramp-up, technology transfer, or process stabilization.

• A hands-on, highly structured, and solution-oriented approach to your tasks.

You thrive on being close to the shop floor, working with operators to ensure that process standards are practical, understood, and followed. You are motivated by establishing structure and stability in a dynamic Greenfield environment, and you maintain a clear perspective—even when working under tight deadlines in an accelerating growth phase.

At FPRT, you are offered a rare career opportunity to shape one of Denmark's most unique industrial and defense-tech projects.
